text:
## Description

Given a collection of fair dice, report the greatest probability that two distinct dice show the same number when rolled independently. Each face is equally likely, and a number can appear on multiple faces of the same die.

## Preconditions

- **PRE-1 (Unverified)** Standard input contains an integer \(N\) from 2 through 100, followed by \(N\) lines describing the dice.
- **PRE-2 (Unverified)** The line for die \(i\) contains a positive integer \(K_i\) followed by exactly \(K_i\) integer face labels. Each label is from 1 through \(10^5\), and the total face count is at most \(10^5\).

## Postconditions

- **POST-1 (Unverified)** The target value is the maximum probability of equal labels over all pairs of distinct dice. Each occurrence of a repeated label contributes its own face probability. Reordering the dice or the faces within a die leaves the target value unchanged.
- **POST-2 (Unverified)** The target value lies between 0 and 1 inclusive. It is 0 exactly when no pair shares a label, and 1 exactly when some pair has the same label on every face of both dice.
- **POST-3 (Unverified)** The Python 3 program prints a numeric answer to standard output. Its absolute or relative error from the target value is at most \(10^{-8}\).

## Test suggestions

- Use two one-face dice with equal labels, then with different labels. Expect 1 and 0, respectively, within the output tolerance (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-2, POST-3).
- Use three dice with face labels \([1,1,2]\), \([1]\), and \([2]\). Expect \(2/3\) within tolerance. Reorder the dice and faces and check the same result (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-1, POST-3).
- Use 100 dice with 1,000 faces each, each die carrying a single repeated label distinct from every other die’s label. Expect 0 within tolerance (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-2, POST-3).

## Unspecified behavior

- Handling of malformed or out-of-range input.
- Numeric formatting beyond the accuracy requirement.
- The identity of a maximizing pair and how ties between pairs are resolved.
